Meaning: The stated policy of the government of a nation regarding the defence of that nation's interest from both local and external threats.

Subject: Defend.
Meaning: Hold and deny to the enemy.

Subject: Defended Position.
Meaning: An area of ground organized for all round defencewhere no indication of the extent of the area or the troops holding it, is given.The levels are:a.Defended Post.Det or sec.b.Defended locality.Pl or coy organized in depth.c.Defended Area.Bn.d.Defended Sector.Bde, div or corps.e.Defended Zone.Army and above level, it has no formations onits flanks.

Subject: Defended Villages.
Meaning: In CRW, Defended Villages are villages in controlledareas which have been organized for defence with a view to giving the inhabitants security from insurgent action, preventing subversive elementsassisting the insurgent and encouraging the provision of information. Initially,defended villages may have to be manned by military forces but in the longterm the aim must be to train and organize home guards so that they and thepolice are able to take over the static defence from military forces.

Subject: Defensive Fire (DF).
Meaning: Pre-arranged fire in the defence which can be brought down quickly on suspected or actual locations of enemy attacking forces.Types of the pre-arranged fire are:a.DFs in Depth.Tasks in depth designed to neutralized and destroy enemy formations at the earliest possible moment.Generally,lies in a beltfrom about1500metresfrom the FEBA and beyond and are coordinated at brigade level.b.Close DFs.Tasks designed to hit the enemy while he is in the FUP, start line or actually assaulting. Close DFs lie approximately200 ''“ 1500metresfrom the FEBA.c.Final Protective Fire (FPF). These are the most important close DFs where enemy threat is greatest or most probable, usually closest to the company localities. They should as much as possible coincide with natural or artificial obstacles, e.g.. Mines, streams, etc. Guns and mortars lays on their FPF when they are not engaging other targets to effect prompt response. A fire unit (filed battery, medium, and mortar section) is allotted one FPF.

Subject: Defensive Minefield.
Meaning: See ''Minefield''.

Subject: Defensive Operation.
Meaning: See ''Operations of War

Subject: Defilade.
Meaning: Protection from hostile ground observation and direct fireprovided by an obstacle such as a hill, ridge or bank. It also implies achievingthis protection through use of artificial obstacles.

Subject: Defiladed Position.
Meaning: A position which is protected naturally fromobservation and fire of flat trajectory weapons.

Subject: Defile.
Meaning: A defile is any natural or artificial feature which caused a body oftroops to contact its normal front during its passage through it. A mountainpass is the most common type of natural defile, a bridge or a raised causewaythrough a marsh, is an example of an artificial defile.

Subject: Dekitting1.
Meaning: Process of withdrawal military effect from military personnelleaving the service.

Subject: Dekitting2.
Meaning: Process of making AFVs vehicles that have just crossed awater obstacle either by swimming or fording, ready for action. It Involveslowering down screens (in screens down areas), and for forded tanks,removal of water proofing equipment (in the dekitting area). Subsequently,post-flotation servicing and checks are carried out.

Subject: Delay Line.
Meaning: A selected report line which requires a delaying force toprevent the enemy from crossing that line until a specified time or theoccurrence of an event.

Subject: Delaying Operation
Meaning: See ''Operations of War''.

Subject: Deliberate Attack.
Meaning: See ''Attack''.

Subject: Deliberate Breaching.
Meaning: The creation of a lane through a minefield or aclear route through a barrier or fortification, which is systematically plannedand carried out.

Subject: Deliberate Crossing.
Meaning: The crossing of an inland water obstacle that requires extensive planning and detailed preparations.

Subject: Demi-Official Letter.
Meaning: 'See Service Correspondence'

Subject: Demobilisation
Meaning: Action taken to return to pre-mobilization status. See''Mobilization''.

Subject: Demolition.
Meaning: Demolition is the destruction of structure with explosives that is of strategic and tactical interest to the military during operation. See 'preliminary demolition target' and 'reserved demolition target'

Subject: Demolition Firing Party.
Meaning: Engineer party with technical responsibility forfiring the demolition.

Subject: Demolition Forms.
Meaning: These are forms prepared by the authorisedcommander's G3 staff and contain orders and coordinating instructions for the demolition guard commander and the firing party commander. They alsocontain procedures for the delegation of authorised powers. These are:a. AF W4012B.An army form containing orders to theCommander Demolition Firing Party to fire both reserved andpreliminary demolitions. It also contains the order to change the Stateof Readiness.b. AF W4012C.An army form containing orders to the demolitionGuard Commander of a reserved demolition.

Subject: Demolition Guard.
Meaning: Demolition Guard is a locally positioned force tasked to ensure demolition site is not captured by the enemy before it is successfully fired. The commander of the demolition guard is responsible for the operational command of all troops at the demolition site, including the demolition firing party. He is responsible for transmitting the order to fire to thedemolition firing party

Subject: Demonstrate.
Meaning: To show by practical example, how a thing is done.

Subject: Demonstration.
Meaning: A show of force on a front where a decision is not sought or made. It is done with the aim of deceiving the enemy.

Subject: Deny.
Meaning: To prevent access by physical presence, blocking, disruption, dislocation and fire.

Subject: Design for Battle.
Meaning: The expression by a commander delivering oral orders of how the intends to fight a battle throughout all its phases. It is in effect a short crisp summary of his chosen course. It is not specific as to particular tasks for formations or units as these are given in detail later.

Subject: Destroy.
Meaning: To kill or so damage an enemy force that it is rendered useless.

Subject: Direct Exchange Line (DEL).
Meaning: A local civil telephone extension connectedvia a PUP to the civil system.

Subject: Direct Fire.
Meaning: Line of sight fire e.g. rifle, tank in primary role.

Subject: Direct Support (DS).
Meaning: The support provided by a unit or formation notattached or under command/control of the supported unit or formation, butrequired to give a priority to the support required by that unit or formation.

Subject: Direct SupportDirected Letter.
Meaning: See 'Service Correspondence'

Subject: Directives.
Meaning: Directives are defined as either 'a military communication inwriting in which policy is established or a specific action is ordered', or 'anycommunication which initiates or governs action, conduct, or procedure'.Adirective is employed at the higher levels of command to initiate activity and togive both general and specific guidance to subordinate commanders.Latitude is given to the addressee to use his discretion on implementing thedirective. There are 3 types of directives: The Command Directive, PolicyDirective and Planning Directives.

Subject: Discipline.
Meaning: Discipline is the art of doing what is right and proper with orwithout supervision. It includes obedience to authority, conformity withregulations, adherence to positive societal norms and values and generalgood conduct in and out of uniform.

Subject: Disengagement Line.
Meaning: In a delay operation, when a large enemy forceapproaches to within a specified distance of a designated report line, then units may move from their delay positions.

Subject: Dislocation.
Meaning: To dislocate the enemy is to deny him the ability to bring his strengths to bear. For example, mounting a hasty attack on an enemy in his FUP prior to launching his attack would dislocate his plans and capability to retain the initiative

Subject: Dispatched Rider (DR).
Meaning: A motorcyclist who dispatches messages.

Subject: Disrupt Effect.
Meaning: A tactical task or obstacle effect (that integrates fireplanning and obstacle effort) that breaks apart an enemy's formation and tempo, interrupts theenemy's timetable, causes premature commitment of forces, or forces him to attack piecemeal.

Subject: Disruption.
Meaning: Disruption is by attacking the enemy selectively to break apart and throw into confusion the assets which are critical to the employment and coherence of his fighting power. For example, an attack on enemy artillery could severely disrupt the enemy's tactical capability.

Subject: Dissemination.
Meaning: The distribution of intelligence in a suitable form to those requiring it, in time for it to be used. It is the last stage of the intelligence Cycle.

Subject: Dissident.
Meaning: An individual who takes covert and overt action against a government.

Subject: Distribution Point.
Meaning: A point located in the fwd BAA where stocks of C-sups are held on wheels by second line transport units from where they will be collected by unit echelons. The allocation of DPs is one per brigade.Depending on the tactical situation, terrain and routes, second line transport may distribute C sups direct to unit locations especially fwd movement of arty ammunition. Distribution points usually carry no stock items; items drawn are issued completely as soon as possible

Subject: Diversion.
Meaning: The act of drawing the attention and forces of an enemy from the point of the principal operation; an attack, or alarm, or feint which divertsattention.

Subject: Divisional Administrative Area(DAA).
Meaning: Administrative area generally located toward the rear of the divisional area which contains unit B echelons and those brigade logistic elements which are notlocated in the forward BAAs and divisional logistic units.The DAA is controlled by rear divisional HQ which may be located in or adjacent to it. The officer responsible for it is nominated by the divisional commander but is usually the G4 staffs. Only 2 ''“ 3 days of supplies are normally held.

Subject: Divisional Support Group D (DSG).
Meaning: A DSG will be established to coordinate and control CSS to the Division. It will be located at the DAA.

Subject: Doctrinal Overlay.
Meaning: In IPB,adoctrinal overlay shows what the friendlyforces and the threat would probably do on a ''flat playing field'' based on their doctrine with no terrain constraints. It is produced on clear unmarked overlays without showing the ''No Go and Slow Go'' areas.

Subject: Doctrine.
Meaning: Military doctrine is fundamental principles by which military forcesguide their action in support of objective. It is authoritative but requires judgment in application

Subject: Document Security.
Meaning: Document security entails all documents to beprotected in accordance with their classification. Distribution of classified documents should be limited to those with a need to know, and deliverymeans assessed for risk.

Subject: Drop Zone.
Meaning: A specified area onto which airborne troops, equipment or supplies are airdropped.

Subject: Dummy Minefield.
Meaning: Another name for Phoney Minefield. See ''Minefield

Subject: Dump.
Meaning: A temporary storage area, usually in the open, for bombs, ammunition, equipment or supplies.

Subject: Dumping.
Meaning: Dumping is the placing of stocks on the ground, additional to reserve stocks normally carried on wheels.

Subject: Dune.
Meaning: A dune is a hill or ridge of sand formed by the wind.

Subject: Dust Distance.
Meaning: Terminology employed in mechanized operations. Means the distance between AFVs in which the dust cloud of a leading AFV does not affect the crew of the following AFV(s). Dust distance will vary according to the nature of country.

Subject: E ''“ Day.
Meaning: The day on which an exercise commences.

Subject: Echelon.
Meaning: The various types of echelon in a Battalion Group are sub-divided as follows:F Echelon.F Echelon comprises all fighting elements of the battalion including all the headquarters and sub-unit logistic assets such as ambulances and fitter sections.A1 Echelon.A1 Echelon is composed of the personnel and vehicles required to provide an immediate or emergency resupply of fuel and ammunition for the battalion at any stage of operations. It may also include the Regimental Aid Post (RAP), if not grouped with F Echelon. It will normally operate centrally under battalion control, but may be placed under sub-unit command when the battalion is operating on a wide frontage.A2 Echelon.Although A2 Echelon will frequently be under brigade command for movement and local defence and will be located with the Brigade Support Group (BSG), it will be under the logistics command of the battalion. It consists of: (1) The remainder of the battalion's combat supply transport and stocks.(2) Technical stores.(3) Repair and recovery resources to augment sub-unit fitter sections.B Echelon.B Echelon consists of the Quartermaster's Department, the Regimental Administration Office and any other elements left out of battle, including battle casualty replacements. It will be located with the Brigade or Divisional Support Groups.

Subject: Effective Range.
Meaning: Confirmed maximum range up to which destructive power is guaranteed for the weapons concerned.

Subject: Effectiveness.
Meaning: The ability of a target audience to respond to apsychological objective. (Used in a psy ops content)'

Subject: Electronic Silence.
Meaning: The deliberate prohibition of electronic radiations,normally applied for a stated period, to specific equipment''™s or frequency bands.

Subject: Electronic Warfare (EW).
Meaning: EW is the military action involving the use ofelectromagnetic energy to determine, exploit, reduce or prevent hostile use of the electromagnetic spectrum and action to retain its effective use by friendlyforces.The components of EW are: EW = ESM (passive offensive) + ECM (active offensive) + EPM (defensive)a.Electronic Warfare Support Measures (ESM).ESM is the principal information gathering and target identification activity of EW. It finds and exploits enemy transmissions and the location of emitters. This applies to both communications and non-communications (radars, lasers etc) transmissions.b.Electronic Counter Measures (ECM).ECM is the prevention of the enemy's use of the electromagnetic spectrum by Electronic Jamming and the use of other forms of Electronic Attack to influence his activities. It is the offensive and active arm of EW and is used to fix and to strike at the enemy.c.Electronic Protective Measures (EPM).EPM is the protection of friendly communications and non-communications systems against the enemy's attempts to find, fix and strike at them.

Subject: Embark.
Meaning: Entry into a ship mainly.

Subject: Embarked Force.
Meaning: That part of an amphibious force that assaults or in the case of minor operations; goes ashore. In a major operation, it should consist of an all arms group and it can expect fire support and logistic support from ships, aircraft and helicopters. The size and grouping of the embarked forcewill depend on the operation and the recourses available.

Subject: Emissions Control (EMCON).
Meaning: EMCON provides selective and controlled use of electro-magnetic, acoustic or other emitters, to optimise command and control while minimizing detection and exploitation of an enemy's sensors.

Subject: Emplacement.
Meaning: A well-fortified gun position or machine gun nest.

Subject: Encirclement.
Meaning: See ''Envelopment''.

Subject: Enclosures.
Meaning: Documents which are complete in themselves and sent with a covering document.

Subject: Encounter Battle.
Meaning: The clearing of opposition either by the Vanguard orAdvance Guard.

Subject: Encounter Crossing.
Meaning: Forcing a passage across a water obstacle lightlyheld by the enemy, off the line of march. Momentum of the advance is thusmaintained. Speedy recce, good engineer intelligence and correct groupingof forces are essential for success. Also known as 'hasty crossing'.

Subject: End State.
Meaning: End State is that state of affairs which needs to be achieved at the end of a campaign either to terminate the conflict or resolve it on favourableterms.

Subject: Enfilade Fire.
Meaning: Fire originating from a flank.

Subject: Engage.
Meaning: In air defence, a fire control order used to direct or authorise units and/or weapon systems to fire on a designated target.

Subject: Envelopment.
Meaning: An offensive action at formation and above level in which the main attack strikes the enemy from the rear. Essentially involves an outflanking movement which passes round or through the enemy positions to cut off his withdrawal routes, line of maintenance and destroy him. Alternatively, the movement may be two-pronged, one element to block the enemy from the front. Envelopment may be single or double:a.Single.Manoeuvre against one flank or around one flank against the rear of the initial disposition of the enemy.b.Double.Otherwise called encirclement. This is envelopmentfrom both flanks simultaneously.

Subject: Equipment.
Meaning: All non-expendable items needed to outfit or equip an individual or organisation.

Subject: Equipment Collection Point.
Meaning: A location usually in or near the forward BAAwhere equipment casualties from units and LADs are collected before back loading by second line recovery resources. It is often convenient to locate it near the FRG (Forward Repair Group).

Subject: Escapee.
Meaning: Any person who after physical capture by the enemy successfully escape into an area under own, friendly or neutral control.

Subject: Escarpment.
Meaning: Escarpment is an extended line of cliffs. That is, ground with sheer drop on one side.

Subject: Escort.
Meaning: A combatant unit(s) assigned to accompany and protect another force or convoy.

Subject: Esprit-De-Corps.
Meaning: That relationship existing in a unit, formation or corps borne out of pride and confidence by all ranks belonging to that unit, formation or corps to the extent that the average soldier believes himself fortunate to belong to a particular unit and feels rather sorry for those soldiers who do not belong. Esprit-de-corps considerably enhance discipline. This is because theindividual is even more ready to sacrifice his own interests for the commongood.

Subject: Espionage.
Meaning: Covert means of obtaining information of the enemy or potential enemy including his future strategic plans.

Subject: Estimate Process..
Meaning: A logical process of reasoning by which a commander considers all the circumstances affecting the military situation and arrives at a decision as to the course of action to be taken in order to accomplish his mission. The types of Estimate Process are:a.The Operational Estimate.The Operational Estimate is designed for a JTFC at the operational level to develop his campaign plan and the subsequent modification of operation orders and directives. The estimate must be command-led, since it is the JTFC's decision that the process supports. All other estimates, at any level should be designed to contribute to the Operational Estimate.b.The Tactical Estimate.The tactical estimate provides a process that can be used by formation headquarters conducting complex planning with time available, within the context of a campaign plan, and where the campaign planning concepts have been decided at the operational level by the JFHQ. As with the joint operational estimate, from which the process has been developed, the tactical estimate seeks to produce a winning concept through analysis that is focused by the JTFC's direction.c. The Combat Estimate.The Combat Estimate is also known as the 7- Questions combat estimate, it is used primarily at the lower tactical level for decision-making in battles and engagements when time is short. It allows the commander at the lower levels of command, especially in the heat of action to use his intuition and training, to compress his decision making to produce a workable plan.

Subject: Estuary.
Meaning: The tidal mouth of a river. A section of a river meeting the sea.

Subject: Evacuation (Evac).
Meaning: The movement of human and equipment causalities out of the area of operations.

Subject: Event Overlay.
Meaning: An event overlay is derived from the situation overlay; it shows graphically the Named Area of Interest (NAI) where key tactical events are likely to take place. Theidentification of these NAIs will prompt the tasking of RISTA to maintainsurveillance over these areas.

Subject: Exchange1.
Meaning: The replacement of clothing and stores items that are either damage or have outlived their usefulness, e.g.., military uniforms.

Subject: Exchange2.
Meaning: Telephone exchange.

Subject: Exchange Point (XP).
Meaning: A point deployed by the highest HQ in anoperation to shorten the turnaround where the replenishment park is too far to the rear for second line transport to get there and back within twenty-four hours.

Subject: Exempt Call.
Meaning: An exempt call is defined as a call to those stations normally designated by a collective or all stations call, less certain specifically exempted stations. It is used when a calling station wishes to call the majority, but not all of the stations associated with a collective or all stations call. Exempt calls can simplify calls and prevent unnecessary replies.

Subject: Exercise.
Meaning: A military manoeuvre or simulated wartime operation involving planning, preparation and execution. It is carried out for the purpose oftraining and evaluation.

Subject: Exploitation1.
Meaning: An offensive operation that usually follows a successful attack and is designed to disorganise the enemy in depth. See ''Core Functions of the Manoeuvrist Approach''.

Subject: Exploitation2.
Meaning: Taking full advantage of success in battle and following up initial gains.

Subject: Exploitation3.
Meaning: Taking full advantage of any information that has come to hand for tactical or strategic purposes.

Subject: Explosive Ordinance.
Meaning: All ammunition containing explosives, nuclear,biological and chemical agents including improvised explosive devices and all similar or related items or components that are explosive in nature.

Subject: Explosive Ordinance Disposal.
Meaning: The detection, identification, field evaluation, rendering safe, recovery and final disposal of unexploded explosive ordnance.

Subject: Extended Defence.
Meaning: A form of positional defence employed on a wide front. It is characterized by large gaps, limited mutual support, greater depth of position and a strong reserve.

Subject: Extraction.
Meaning: In amilitary operation, extraction is the urgent removal of an individual or a group of individuals or materiel from a threat.

Subject: F Hour.
Meaning: The time designated for the start of FLOT aviation operations.

Subject: Facsimile (Fax).
Meaning: A facility for transmitting a document e.g., map, table or diagram over a voice circuit.

Subject: Fall Out1.
Meaning: To dismiss a soldier(s) from a superior officer's/NCO's imm presence.

Subject: Fall Out2.
Meaning: Radioactive materials deposited on the surface of the earth following the explosion of nuclear weapons, not only in the immediate vicinityof the explosion but over any region of the globe.

Subject: Favourable Air Situation.
Meaning: That degree of dominance in the air battle of oneforce over another, which permits the conduct of operations by the former and its related land, sea and air forces at a given time and place, withoutprohibitive interference by the opposing air force.

Subject: Feint Attack.
Meaning: The purpose of a feint attack is to distract the action of an enemy force by seeking contact with it.

Subject: Field Ambulance.
Meaning: Medical unit that provides second line medical cover to units, it is allocated on a scale of one per brigade. It is fully mobile on organic transport and carries sufficient tentages to enable it work in the field whensuitable buildings are not available.In war, a field ambulance normally establishes one dressing station; the Main Dressing Station (MDS), wherecasualties receive treatment, are documented and prepared for future evacuation. The MDS in this case is normally sited in the fwd BAA. Sometimes however, in order to meet operational exigencies, a field ambulance can as an exception, provide two dressing stations, the MDS and the Advance Dressing Station (ADS).This is to cover long communication lines characteristic of the Advance and Withdrawal operations of war. In this case, it is normal for the ADS to be located in the fwd BAA and the MDS in the BAA.

Subject: Field Artillery.
Meaning: Branch of artillery that is concerned with finding andengaging ground targets with indirect fire support of infantry and armour.Provides 'Close Support' and General Support.

Subject: Field Craft.
Meaning: The basic field training given to an individual soldier to enable is take his proper place in the military team under operational conditions. It includes the basic fundamentals of fire and movement, observationjudging distance, seeing without being seen and hearing without being heard andcamouflage and concealment. It also includes how to make the best possible use of cover and how to move with weapons and equipment.

Subject: Field of Fire.
Meaning: An area in which it will be possible to fire effectively from a given position and which is related to a particular weapon.

Subject: Field Post Office.
Meaning: Postal facility established in the Combat Zone.

Subject: Field signals.
Meaning: Field signals are alternative means of passing orders and controlling troops by the use of hands, limbs, weapons and whistle when voice control is not possible owing to; battle noises, need for silence and intervening distances being too much for effective voice control.

Subject: Field Surgical Team.
Meaning: See ''Advance Surgical Centre''.

Subject: Fighter Ground Attack (FGA).
Meaning: Aircraft used for close air support mission.

Subject: Fighting Power.
Meaning: Fighting power defines an army ability to fight. It isexpressed in qualitative terms, reflecting the suitability for employment in a particular environment of operations. Fighting power is made up of 3 components; conceptual, physical and moral components.a.Conceptual Components.This can be described as the thought process behind the ability to fight. It is made up of Principles of war, military doctrine and development.b.The Moral Component.The moral component concerns with the ability to get people to fight. It will involve; motivation, leadership and management.c.The Physical Component.The physical component is the means to fight. It is the equivalent of the term'combat power'(see'combat power').Physical componentincludesthe following elements; manpower, equipment, logistics/sustainability, training and readiness.

Subject: Final Assault Position.
Meaning: Area close to the objective where assaulting troops,it not already so deployed adopt their formation for the final assault. It may not be possible to lay down the precise positions at orders and is more likely to be indicated by radio or verbally during the attack.

Subject: Final Protective Fire.
Meaning: See Defensive Fire

Subject: Find.
Meaning: See Core Functions of the Manoeuvrist Approach.

Subject: Fire and Manoeuvre.
Meaning: The principle of having one 'leg' on the groundproviding security and providing fire or being ready to fire, while the other 'leg' moves (i.e., one leg up, one down). The idea is to ensure a proper balanceand close coordination of fire power (including air support) with the tactical mobility of the combat arms for the successful execution of a ground battle.

Subject: Fire Coordination Area (FCA).
Meaning: FCA is an area subject to specific restraintsinto which fire support in excess of those restraints (weight of fire, types of ammo etc) will not be delivered without the prior approval of the authorityestablishing the restraint.

Subject: Fire for Effect.
Meaning: 'Fire for effect' means produce the full weight of fire requested in initial orders. This term is applicable to indirect fire and is issued after satisfactory ranging.

Subject: Fire Mission1.
Meaning: Initial warning order when requesting for fire, transmitted over the radio by an observer (supported arm, e.g. Infantry) to an OP officer (Artyofficer to whom fire request is made).

Subject: Fire Mission2.
Meaning: Specific assignment given to a fire unit as part of a definite plan.

Subject: Fire Plan.
Meaning: Plan involving the dovetailing of available supporting firerecourses (including tank fire) to achieve the best possible utilization of theweapons in support of a unit or formation.

Subject: Fire Support Cell (FSC).
Meaning: A Cell where detailed planning, control andcoordination of fire support is carried out at battalion group level. The FSC is supervised by the BC of the Direct Support battery who advises the battaliongroup commander on all fire support matters.The BC is assisted by the support company commander or mortar platoon commander. The FSC is also responsible for air safety within the battalion group air space and might include a forward air controller (FAC).

Subject: Fire Support Coordination Line (FSCL).
Meaning: A line established by theappropriate ground commander to ensure coordination of fire not under hiscontrol but which may affect current tactical operations.The FSCL is used tocoordinate fire of air, ground or sea weapon systems using any type ofammunition against surface targets.

Subject: Fire Support Coordination Measure (FSCM).
Meaning: Measure taken to coordinate the fire of disparate fire units and to minimise fratricide.

Subject: Fire trench.
Meaning: Fire trench is that part of a battle trench from which the enemy may be observed and engaged.

Subject: Fire Unit.
Meaning: The minimum number of weapons that can be employed on anyone serial of a fire plan. Below this level, fire is considered largely ineffective. A fire unit may be:a. One field battery (but four guns can be used for a smoke serial and only two for illumination).b. A troop of a medium battery (because of their heavier shells).c. A platoon of tanks.d. Two fighter ground attack (FGA) aircraft.

Subject: First Line Scale.
Meaning: The quantity of C sups which is normally held by a unit on first line (i.e., organic) transport. It iscalculated to sustain that units in operations for a specific length of time without re-supply. It is controlled by the unit commander. If unit transport cannot carry the first line scale, the balance is either dumped in or near the unit's location or carried by second line transport.

Subject: First Line Stock.
Meaning: See ''Operating Stock''.

Subject: Fitted For Radio (FFR).
Meaning: Vehicle made according to specifications to carryradios and operate as vehicular stations, e.g., FFR Land Rover.

Subject: Fitter.
Meaning: Automotive and gunnery repairman

Subject: Fix.
Meaning: See ''Core Functions of the Manoeuvrist Approach''.

Subject: Fix Effect.
Meaning: A tactical obstacle effect that integrates fire planning and obstacle effort to slow down an attacker within a specified area, normally an engagement area.

Subject: Fixed Line
Meaning: A fixed line is a given line and point of aim on which a weapon is capable of firing from during mist, darkness or under poor visibility. It is notnecessary for the target to be visible when a weapon is set on fixed line as the weapon is so sited that its fire is effective on a selected area of ground. Fire onfixed line is opened on a pre-arranged signal order.

Subject: Flag March..
Meaning: A foot march by soldiers (sometimes displaying military hardware including AFVs) in a civilian environment either to sell the military profession to civilians or in a CRW environment to serve as a deterrent topotential troublemakers

Subject: Flank Guard.
Meaning: A security element operating to the flank of a moving or stationary force to protect it from enemy ground observation, direct fire, and surprise attack.

Subject: Flank Protection.
Meaning: The means by which enemy interference by fire or assault onto the flanks of own force(s) is dealt with.

Subject: Flat Trajectory Weapons.
Meaning: Direct fire weapons with line of sight aiming e.g., 107mm Anti-Tank gun etc.

Subject: Force Correlation.
Meaning: This is a table (Relative Strength Table) comparing the strength of friendly and threat forces, at agreed intervals, to determine whether or not a force has achieved desired norms.

Subject: Foreshore.
Meaning: Foreshore is that portion of the shore between high and low watermarks.

Subject: Fording.
Meaning: Fording is the movement of a vehicle on the bed of awaterobstacle. A certain amount of preparation is usually carried out on the vehicle,depending on the depth of the water. For tanks and AFVs, fording may be:a.Shallow.No preparation is required for the vehicle. Top of the engine compartment and exhaust opening remain outside the water.b.Medium.Water level is up to turret ring. Preliminary preparations like sealing the top of the engine compartment and fitting special one-way valves on the exhaust are required. The driver will have to be directed by the tank commander.c.Deep.Otherwise called immersed fording or snorkelling. The tank is completely submerged. Air forintake by the engine and breathing by crew is introduced by snorkel apparatus. The drivermaintains direction by gyrocompass or by guidance via the radio, from outside.

Subject: Formal Letter.
Meaning: See 'Service Correspondence'

Subject: Formation.
Meaning: Brigade, division and corps are all referred to individually as formation.

Subject: Forming Up Place(FUP).
Meaning: The last position occupied by the assault echelonbefore crossing the start line/line of departure.

Subject: Forward Air Controller (FAC).
Meaning: An officer, warrant officer or senior NCO who from a forward ground or air position, directs the action of combat aircraft engaged in offensive close air support of land force.

Subject: Forward Brigade Administrative Area (Fwd BAA).
Meaning: Area which contains battalion A2 echelons and in addition may contain elements of logistic units,some of which would be under divisional control, which must be deployed in the brigade area in order to operate efficiently, e.g., DP. All units in the fwd BAA are controlled by the brigade HQ.

Subject: Forward Edge of Battle Area (FEBA).
Meaning: FEBA is the foremost limit of areawhere ground combat troops are deployed, excluding areas which the covering troops/screening forces are operating, designated to coordinate firesp and positioning of forces or the manoeuvre of units.

Subject: Forward Line of Troops (FLOT
Meaning: FLOT is the line which indicates the most fwd positions of friendly forces in any kind of military operations at a specific time.

Subject: Forward Mounting Base (FMB).
Meaning: A secure base, port or airfield, from whichan operation may be launched. It is normally, but not necessarily, external to the theatre of operations and may be an essential stepping-stone into thattheatre.

Subject: Forward Observation Officer (FOO).
Meaning: The Arty Officer in an OP, when the OP is mobile, e.g., in an advance, a field battery produces 3 FOOs.

Subject: Forward Operational Base.
Meaning: An area providing a semi-permanent firm base from which offensive action against the insurgents can be developed. It should be established at a seat of local government as, a formation base, usually at brigade level, and will normally have a Tactical Transport (Medium range or short range) airfield, capable of quick development.

Subject: Forward Passage of Lines.
Meaning: An operation in which a force advances or attacks through another force which is in contact with theenemy. The force in contact remains in place and must provide the advancing force with as muchassistance as possible including tactical and logistical support. A forward passage of lines will be used when:a.An attack is to be continued with fresh or more suitable forces.b.The force to be relieved is closely engaged with the enemy.c.The advancing force has to take possession of suitable terrain in order to continue the battle.

Subject: Forward Rally.
Meaning: An area under cover in the vicinity of an objective to which tanks go when released from dominating the objective, and from which they are immediately available to return to fire positions or to support counterattacks.

Subject: Forward Repair Group (FRG).
Meaning: A repair organization provided by an armoured or infantry workshop to carry our priority second line repairs in forward units. The FRG is based on forward repair teams (FRT) - four FRTs forinfantry workshops, considerably more for armoured workshops. The FRG is formed by adding elements from the MT platoon and the stores section NAOCto the FRTs provided by the repair company.

Subject: Forward Repair Section (FRS).
Meaning: A workshop repair section of up to 50 men formed by base workshop and deployed usually to carry out unit and field repairs in an emergency.

Subject: Forward Repair Teams (FRT).
Meaning: Repair elements of the FRG that carry out priority tasks like replacement of major assemblies in forward units locations. Each FRT consist of up to four tradesmen mounted in a vehicle capable oflifting major assemblies up to three tones for an armoured workshop and up to one tone for an Infantry workshop.

Subject: Four Ds.
Meaning: These are the 4 fundamental questions which need to beaddressed if logistic requirements are to be assessed they are the start point.of all CSS planning. These are:Destination,Demand,DistanceandDuration.a.Destination.The destination sets the overall environment in which the operation is to take place,which determines the conditions for the pattern of wear and tear on equipment, the physiological demands on troops and define the strategic L of C.b.Demand.Demand encompasses the rate of consumption and usage of materiel, it stems directly from the commander's intent.c.Distance.Distance req consideration not only of the strategic L of C, but also of that within the theatre before, during and after the operation. The length, capacity and topography of the L of C will determine the size, shape, structure and balance of the CSS resources committed to it.d.Duration.The length of operations and rate of demand will determine the overall volume of materiel necessary or the size of the logistic problem. It will specify the endurance requirements, the needto rotate or replace equipment and men, and medical holding policies.

Subject: Fragmentary Order (FragO).
Meaning: A FragO may be written, graphical/schematic,oral or a combination of these methods. It is used to supplement or amend an operation order. It should follow the same paragraph format as the orderwhich it is to supplement or amend. Where there is ''no change'' to a paragraph it must be annotated as such.

Subject: Fratricide.
Meaning: Fratricide is the unintentional killing or wounding of friendly personnel by fire.

Subject: Frontal Attack.
Meaning: An offensive manoeuvre in which the main effort is directed against the front of the enemy force(s).

Subject: Full Command.
Meaning: See 'State of Command'.

Subject: Full Service Marching Order (FSMO).
Meaning: This is combat order (see) plusrucksack and is a load which will be required for an operation of up to twoweeks duration without resupply except for ammunition, rations and water.

Subject: Functional Command.
Meaning: A command based on military functions ratherthan geographic areas.

Subject: Functional Control.
Meaning: The authority vested in a commander of one of the Services, a specialist agency or MOD branch acting on behalf of aServiceBoard.

Subject: Functions in Combat.
Meaning: Functions in Combat are practical conceptualtools deduced from principles of war required to implement ManoeuvristApproach to operations. The 6 principal functions in combat are:a.Information and Intelligence.Accurate and timely intelligence is fundamental to the success of all operations. Much of this information is derived from Reconnaissance, Intelligence, Surveillance and Target Acquisition (RISTA).b.Manoeuvre.To manoeuvre is to seek to get into a position of advantage in respect of the enemy from which force can be threatened or applied.c.Firepower.Firepower destroys, neutralises and suppresses; it is essential in defeating an enemy's ability to fight.d.Protection.Protection preserves the fighting potential of a force so that it can be applied at a decisive time and place.e.Combat Service Support (CSS).CSS sustains the force. It is the support provided to combat forces primarily in the fields of personnel and logistics.f.Command.Command is the exercise of authority and direction by a designated commander for the planning, direction, coordination and control of a military force.

Subject: G Day/Hour.
Meaning: The day and/or time on which an order (normally national) is given to deploy a unit.

Subject: Gamble.
Meaning: Military gamble is an operation which can lead either to victory or the complete destruction of one's force. It is an operation of great risk, for instant, when defeat is imminent and gaining time is pointless, the only chance left is a ''gamble''.

Subject: General Duties (GD).
Meaning: Non-technical duties.

Subject: General Purpose Transport (GT).
Meaning: Five and ten tone trucks required to move men and materials from the rear areas into the Combat Zone. It is from these transport resources that ST companieswill move combat supplies forward from RP to XP and further to the DP.

Subject: General Support (Gen Sp).
Meaning: That support which is given to the supportedforce as a whole and not to any particular sub-division thereof. Often used to refer to artillery which is used to influence the corps or divisional battle andnormally tasked for counter battery and other depth targets. There is no guarantee of fire to the manoeuvre arm.

Subject: General Support Reinforcing (Gen Sp Rft).
Meaning: Gen Sp Rft artillery has the mission of supporting the forces as a whole and, on a secondary basis, ofproviding reinforcing fire for another artillery unit. Artillery allocated in this role has two priorities: the first is to the Comd Arty and the second is to thesupported formation. It provides therefore a certain degree of guaranteed fire though it is likely to have an ammunition caveat.

Subject: General War.
Meaning: An unrestricted conflict between major powers. This might include widespread use of nuclear, chemical and possibly biological weapons.

Subject: Geneva Conventions 1949.
Meaning: Those regulations governing the treatment and handling of prisoners of war (POWs). POWs are expected to be treated firmly, fairly and humanely.

Subject: Genocide.
Meaning: The systematic killing of all the people from a national, ethnic, or religious group, or an attempt to do this.

Subject: Go.
Meaning: In conducting IPB,''Go'' areas are grounds which are open and suitable for manoeuvre. It must be assessed according to the type of force, forexample, what is ''Go'' to the dismounted forces might not be ''Go'' to the armour or mounted forces.

Subject: Gorge.
Meaning: A gorge is a deep narrow valley which is rugged and usually rocky.

Subject: Grand/National Strategy.
Meaning: See 'Strategy'Grid.Grid is a system of squares formed by lines, which representing progressive distances EAST and NORTH of a fixed point.Grid Bearing.The direction of an object from a point, expressed as an angle (degree or mil) measured clockwise with reference to grid north.Ground of Tactical Importance (GTI).GTI is the ground the possession of which by the end willseriously interfere with the successful def of the position.

Subject: Ground Manoeuvre Forces.
Meaning: There are three types of ground manoeuvreforces: Heavy, medium and light. They will usually operate in combination.a.Heavy Forces.Heavy forces are basically heavy armoured fighting vehicles, they utilise automotive power to deploy considerable firepower, protection and battlefield mobility. Although, their use is restricted in some complex terrain, and their operational and strategic mobility is constrained by weight and logistic requirements, they still form a major component of many land forces.b.Medium Forces.Medium forces are basically light armoured vehicles they are strategically and operationally more deployable than heavy forces, and may be among the first elements to deployinto a theatre.c.Light Forces.Light forces are basically foot infantry troops, they have significant strategic mobility, since they can be transported by aircraft to any theatre. They may be the only forces that canoperate in complex terrain. However, their firepower is limited compared to heavy or medium forces, and they are vulnerable. Provision of greater mobility or firepower (APC) gives them the characteristics of medium forces, but may reduce their strategicmobility and utility.

Subject: Ground Surveillance Plan.
Meaning: The plan to coordinate the employment of patrols, Ops, FOO and MFC zones of observations, aerial recce and surveillance devices. This is to enable the commander watch the battlefield at all times and gather combat intelligence in time for him to react and retain the initiative.

Subject: Ground Zero.
Meaning: The point on the ground surface vertically beneath or above which a nuclear weapon has exploded. Maximum damage from the nuclear explosion will be recorded on the Ground Zero.

Subject: Group Training.
Meaning: Combined arms training from company group level.

Subject: Grouping.
Meaning: Allotment of arms and services under one commander for a task.

Subject: Grouping System.
Meaning: This is the division of a battlegroup into functional groupsto achieve effective concurrent activity prior to an operation, The compositionof each group will vary according to the task, as explained below:a.Reconnaissance Group (R Group).The RG ro up is responsible for reconnaissance and planning. The group includes those necessary to give the appropriate advice, a security element and communications.b.Orders Group (O Group).The O Group receives orders and contains all those with a part to play in the forthcoming operation. From these orders, recipients extract the appropriate information and issue their own orders. may undertake preliminary moves, whilst orders are being written and given.d.Harbour and Rear Recce Parties.If the main body has to move forward to a concentration or assembly area, a harbour party will be despatched ahead of the main body. Its tasks will be to recceand lay out the new area and then to guide the main body, as they arrive, to their positions. If it is necessary for a battlegroup to withdraw, it is usual to despatch a rear recce group. This group combines a tactical reconnaissance function with that of the normal harbour party in the event of having to fight from this position upon their arrival.

Subject: Guard.
Meaning: Guards are covering troops deployed to delay the en for a specifiedperiod, additional to observation and report on en movement.

Subject: Guard Tank.
Meaning: Tank designated for 'sentry' tasks in a combat team leaguer.The tank remains fully manned for the period it so designated.

Subject: Guerrilla Warfare.
Meaning: Military or Para-military operations conducted in enemy held or hostile territory by irregular, predominantly indigenous force. Guerrillawarfare will be the main preoccupation of security forces in counter insurgency.

Subject: Guided Weapon.
Meaning: Weapons in which the projectiles are remotely guided by an external mechanism onto a target after firing. In some cases, the weapons are fed with relevant dataand the projectiles take over the guidance automatically and home on to their targets.

Subject: H-Hour.
Meaning: a. The specific time at which an operation or exercise commences or is due to commence. It is also the time at which the Line of Departure (LD) is crossed by the leading elements in an attack.b. In amphibious operations, the time at which the first waterborne wave of an amphibious assault lands on the beach.

Subject: Hachuring.
Meaning: Hachuring is a conventional method of representing hill features by short disconnected lines drawn directly down the slope in the direction of the flow of water on the slopes.

Subject: Hand-Over Line(HL).
Meaning: A control feature, preferably following easily definedterrain features, at which responsibility for the conduct of combat operations is passed from one force to another.

Subject: Harbour.
Meaning: An area well out of contact where a force lie up for any length of time for administrative convenience (e.g. refit, rest, reorganization and maintenance). Protection and concealment will be maintained.

Subject: Harbour Party.
Meaning: A party formed when required for a specific task, e.g. recce and planning of a new harbour area (See ''Grouping System''). On completion of the task, members rejoin their normal echelons. At battalion level, it will be commanded by the 2ic and will include representatives of the company groups and specialist subunits.

Subject: Hasty Attack.
Meaning: In land operations, an attack in which preparation time is traded for speed in order to exploit an opportunity.

Subject: Hasty Breaching.
Meaning: The rapid creation of a route through a minefield, barrier or fortification by any expedient method.

Subject: Hasty Crossing.
Meaning: The crossing of an inland water obstacle using thecrossing means at hand or those readily available and made without pausing for elaborate preparations.

Subject: Hasty Defence.
Meaning: A defence normally organised while in contact with the enemy or when contact is imminent and time available for the organisation is limited. It is characterised by improvement of the natural defensive strength of the terrain by utilisation of foxholes, emplacements, and obstacles.

Subject: Headquarters.
Meaning: The word headquarters is often used as a generic term for the grouping of the staff, its associated CIS and a structure which provides a working environment. There are 6 types of headquarters and they are described below:a.Main Headquarters (Main).As the name implies this is the central controlling headquarters (at any level) where all the staff functions of that headquarters are coordinated and where thecommand and control of all subordinate units is focussed. The headquarters itself is normally commanded by the COS who decides on its composition, organisation, siting and tactical deployment.b.Forward Headquarters (Fwd HQ).This is usually an advance or detached element of the HQ, perhaps deployed early into theatre, with a skeleton communications infrastructure and very limited protection. It would typically be mounted in soft-skinned vehicles. Fwd HQ lacks the resources to support command in battle.c.Tactical Headquarters (Tac HQ).All field headquarters requireto be tactical. If a headquarters has become too large and unwieldy, then its structure should be pruned. Tac HQ refers to a small HQ (Comd and principal Arms Advisers as appropriate) complete withsufficient mobility, protection and communications to command the battle for limited periods away from Main.d.Alternate Headquarters (Alt HQ).Alternate headquarters provide continuity of command when a headquarters either needs to be moved or is put out of action.e.Step-Up Headquarters (Step-Up).If fewer vehicles, manpower and CIS are available, a Step-Up headquarters may replicate only key functions and be capable of holding control for only limited periods while a Main headquarters moves and while men andvehicles are transferred from the previous Main headquarters location.f.Rear Headquarters (Rear).The principal location for the designated commander of any rear operations including combat service support activity.

Subject: Hide.
Meaning: Hide is a concealed position in which a force waits before operation or before moving into battle position. A subunit hide should provide:a. Overhead protection (OHP) and concealment against en action and observation.b. All round defence.c. Dispersion.d. Easy access and breakout.

Subject: High Pay-Off Target (HPT).
Meaning: HPTs are those targets/assets whoseacquisition and successful attack will contribute substantially to the successof the friendly commander's mission.

Subject: High Pay-Off Target List (HPTL).
Meaning: A HPTL is a list of HPTs in priority.

Subject: High Value Target (HVT)
Meaning: HVTs are those targets/assets which the enemycommander requires for the successful completion of his mission and are,therefore, of high value to him.

Subject: Hold.
Meaning: Hold is applicable to both defence and attack.a.In defence.To hold is to maintain or retain possession of a position or an area by force.b.In an attack.Holding Attack is to exert sufficient pressure to hold the enemy in position to deceive him as to where the main attack is coming from. This is to prevent movement, re-disposition of enemyforces and also to prevents him from reinforcing his elements and /or to cause him to commit reserves prematurely at an indecisive location.

Subject: Homer.
Meaning: Homer is a process where an aircraft, using the homing facility, can home on to any VHF/FM station within range by getting the station to transmitvoice or a carrier wave for short periods. Homing facility are used when a pilot has difficulty in locating a station on theground. Homing indications will only be seen while the ground station is transmitting.

Subject: Horizontal Equivalent (HE).
Meaning: The distance measured on the map betweenadjacent contours or between two points.

Subject: Host Nation Support (HNS).
Meaning: Civil and military assistance rendered inpeace and war by a host nation to allied forces which are located on or in transit through the host nation's territory. The basis of such assistance is commitments arising from bilateral or multilateral agreements concluded between the host nation and the nation(s) having forces operating on the hostnation's territory.

Subject: Howitzer.
Meaning: A gun with a high angle (450800) capability, giving it the same ability as mortars in engaging targets on reverse slopes, etc.

Subject: Hull Down.
Meaning: Normal tank position for direct fire, only the turret is visible to the enemy.

Subject: Identification Friend or Foe (IFF).
Meaning: A system using electromagnetic transmissions to which equipment carried by friendly forces automatically responds, for example by emitting pulses, thereby distinguishing themselves from enemy forces

Subject: Illumination Attack.
Meaning: The use of white light at any stage of a night attack.

Subject: Image Intensifier (II).
Meaning: II is a passive device used to make objects visible indarkness. The II principle basically involves the use of ambient light to intensify the image of the objects electronically, thereby making the objects visible.

Subject: Immediate Air Support.
Meaning: Air support to meet specific requests which ariseduring the course of a battle, and which by their nature cannot be planned in advance as opposed to pre-planned air support for which notification is madein advance (normally forty-eight hours in advance).

Subject: Important Ground
Meaning: Ground that is highly desirable rather than essentialto hold.

Subject: Imprest Account.
Meaning: An imprest account is the account maintained in acommand into which all public funds released to the command to meet expenditure under the approved Army allocation is paid. The purpose of imprest account is to record receipts and subsequent expenditure of the funds into it.

Subject: In Direct Support (Artillery).
Meaning: Implies the fire or locating effort of the arty unitis normally guaranteed and arty liaison is provided at every level of command (e.g. FOO at Coy level, BC at Bn-level, etc). Thus an arty unit or subunit canonly be placed in direct support of one battalion group or formation. Arty in direct support provides:a. Advice and communication to the supported arm.b. Observation (if applicable) to the front and flanks.c. Guaranteed fire support from its guns.

Subject: In Support.
Meaning: An expression used to denote the task of providing artillery supporting fire to a formation or unit. Liaison and observation are not normally provided.

Subject: Individual Training.
Meaning: All forms of training of the soldier, NCO, warrant officer and officer as an individual to enable each take his proper place and play his part adequately in his arm or service. Some of the aspects of individualtraining in the infantry for example include physical fitness training, shooting and weapon handling, communication skills, helicopter drills, preparation offire and shelter trenches and overhead protection, night training, AFV and aircraft recognition, field craft, general knowledge, etc. Some of these aspects are common to all arms and services.

Subject: Indoctrination.
Meaning: A methodical process of interrogation, discussion,propaganda and harassment designed to alter people's concepts and convictions and to condition them to accepting a new ideology or thinking.

Subject: Infantry.
Meaning: The Infantry mission is 'to close with and engage the enemy in concert with other arms, through fire and manoeuvre in all operational theatres and environments, in order to bring about his defeat'

Subject: Infantry Combat Vehicle (ICV).Infantry Predominant or
Meaning: Modified APC that not only carries theinfantry to the battlefield, but also into it. The main modification is onincreased armament, thereby giving the infantry more teeth.

Subject: Infantry Heavy
Meaning: See 'Armour Predominant'.

Subject: Infantry Telephone.
Meaning: Telephone mounted at the rear of the hull of a tank tofacilitate infantry men from outside the tank speaking with individual tank commanders within. Not all tanks carry infantry telephones.

Subject: Infiltration.
Meaning: A technique and process in which a force moves asindividuals or small groups over, through or around enemy positions without detection

Subject: Information.
Meaning: Unprocessed or 'raw' data which may either be used simply to inform about some matter or, which can be subjected to an analytical process, in order to assess a capability or predict what the outcome of an event may be.

Subject: Information Security (INFOSEC).
Meaning: INFOSEC is the security of InformationSystems (IS), including hardware, software and bearer systems. Particularattention should be paid to IS using commercial bearer systems, such as theInternet.

Subject: Informant.
Meaning: A person who provides information to a collection agency. See 'Sources and Agencies'.

Subject: Informer.
Meaning: A member of an organisation who passes information to the opponents of the organization.

Subject: Infra Red (IR).
Meaning: Active night fighting device which enables the user to see in darkness, also called red light. The system depends upon emitting an IR beam which is invisible to the naked eye but when viewed through special IRviewing device appears as light. It can be detected by an enemy with an IR capability.

Subject: Infra Red Line Scan (IRLS).
Meaning: IRLS is a sensor employed by reconnaissanceaircraft to detect natural infrared radiation on the ground. It is of particular value in the jungle because of its ability to penetrate natural cover althoughwater vapour in the atmosphere tends to degrade the resolution obtained.

Subject: Installation.
Meaning: Any logistic or administrative base. This definition also includes POW camps.

Subject: Instructions.
Meaning: An instruction is used to regulate military activity, itcomplement directives or orders. Examples are:a.Standing Instructions. Standing Instructions are issued typically to set out organisational responsibilities and to govern routine administrative procedures and actions.b.Periodic Instructions.Periodic Instructions cater for anyspecific actions required of a non-routine nature.c.Formal Instructions.Formal Instructions carry authorityequivalent to that of directives or orders.

Subject: Insurgency.
Meaning: A form of rebellion in which a dissident faction that has the support or acceptance of a substantial part of the population instigates thecommission of widespread acts of civil disobedience, sabotage and terrorism, and wages guerrilla warfare in order to overthrown a government. A state of insurgency implies that the insurgents have control of sizeable areas of the country and that it will almost inevitably be part of a revolutionary war on the communist pattern.

Subject: Insurgent.
Meaning: Insurgent is a term that can be used in place of any of these following terms when applicable, these are; guerrilla, revolutionary, terrorist, dissident, rioter, saboteur, enemy, insurrectionist or rebel.

Subject: Insurrection (Revolt) and Rebellion.
Meaning: When subject revolt they openly express their dissatisfaction with the established government or policies. When such an expression is armed and organized it becomes a rebellion. When a rebellion has a large measure of support and aims to overthrow the government a state of insurgency exists.

Subject: Intelligence.
Meaning: A prediction or assessment resulting from the collection, evaluation, analysis, integration and interpretation of all available information.

Subject: Intelligence Briefing.
Meaning: One of the methods of disseminating intelligencegiven in a set sequence to ensure that no important details are omitted. The intelligence briefing must include 'Comment' and an overall summary of enemy capabilities. The complete format is contained in appropriate service manuals appertaining to 'Intelligence'.

Subject: Intelligence Cycle.
Meaning: This is the process by which information is turned intointelligence and disseminated. It consists of 5 stages which, although cyclical in nature, may also take place concurrently. They are summarised as follows:a.Direction.The commander produces his intelligence requirements.b.Tasking.The G2 staff task appropriate sources and agencies with specific question.c.Collection.Sources and agencies collect information or provide intelligence.d.Processing.Information is collated, evaluated, analysed, integrated and interpreted by the G2 staff. The product of this processing is intelligence.e.Dissemination.Information and intelligence are passed or presented to those who need it.

Subject: Intelligence Estimate.
Meaning: A written appreciation by the intelligence staffconsidered solely from the enemy's point of view. The intelligence staff musttherefore 'think as the enemy thinks'. The estimate is made assuming theworst case, i.e., that the enemy is aware of our capabilities and intentions.The aim is to ultimately arrive at the most probable enemy COA in the givencircumstance.

Subject: Intelligence Preparation of the Battlefield (IPB).
Meaning: IPB is a systematic and continuous process of analyzing environment in a specific geographic areaand the threat. IPB identifies critical battlefield decision points, so that Reconnaissance, Intelligence,Surveillance and Target Acquisition (RISTA) assets can be used to best effect, in order to assist the commander in making his decision. IPB has 3 main steps; these are battlefield area evaluation, threat evaluation and threat integration.

Subject: Intelligence Report (INTREP).
Meaning: A non-routine report, initiated at any level,containing urgent information or intelligence that cannot await the next routine report. Whenever an interpretation of the information given in themassage is included, it should be preceded by the word 'Comment'.

Subject: Intelligence Summary (INTSUM).
Meaning: A routine report initiated at brigade and above levels and contains all important items of information and intelligence within the period covered, including relevant negative information. It has no format except that:a. The text of an INTSUM is preceded by the abbreviation INTSUM.b. The intelligence staff's deduction is preceded by the word 'Comments'.

Subject: Intelligence, Surveillance, Target Acquisition and Reconnaissance(ISTAR).
Meaning: See ''Reconnaissance Intelligence, Surveillance, Target Acquisition'' (RISTA).

Subject: Interception
Meaning: Interception is the act of searching for, listening to and recording radio communications and electronic transmissions for the purpose of obtaininginformation.

Subject: Interchangeability.
Meaning: A condition which exists when two or more itemspossess such functional and physical characteristics as to be equivalent in performance and durability, and are capable of being exchanged one for theother without alteration of the items or of adjoining items, except for adjustment and without selection for fit and performance.

Subject: Intercommunications.
Meaning: Internal communications, by telephone or radio.May be within a HQ, an establishment, or a vehicle.

Subject: Interdiction.
Meaning: Actions to divert, disrupt, delay, or destroy the enemy before he can affect friendly forces.

Subject: Interface.
Meaning: The common bdry between a system or mode of op and a different system or mode.

Subject: Interlocking Fire.
Meaning: Firing across another subunit's weapon fire. The aim is to ensure that the arcs of responsibility of the small arms of neighbouring subunits cross in order to avoidleaving a gap between sub units. Overlapping fire on the other hand takes care of the neighbouring subunits frontages.

Subject: Intermediate Objective.
Meaning: In land warfare, an area or feature between the line of departure and an objective which must be seized or held.

Subject: Intermediate Position.
Meaning: A delaying position temporarily occupied by troops to cover a withdrawal and buy time to allow for the preparation and occupation of a new main defensive position.

Subject: Internal Security.
Meaning: Any military role which involves primarily themaintenance and restoration of law and order and essential services in the face of civil disturbances and disobedience, using minimum force. It coversaction dealing with minor civil disorders with no political undertones as well as riots devouring of revolts and even the early stages of rebellion.

Subject: International Maritime Satellite System (INMARSAT).
Meaning: Fixed and portable systems extensively used for speech and data transmission in nonhostileoperations e.g.humanitarian relief ops.

Subject: Interoperability.
Meaning: The ability of systems, units or forces to provide services to and accept services from other systems, units or forces and to use the services so exchanged to enable them to operate effectively together.

Subject: Interrogation.
Meaning: Questioning, mainly of POWs and suspects.

Subject: Intimate Support Tanks.
Meaning: Those tanks in an infantry/tank attack which assault the objective with the infantry from a fire base using direct fire.

Subject: Intruder Operations.
Meaning: Offensive air operations by day or night over enemyterritory with the primary object of destroying enemy aircraft in the vicinity of their bases.

Subject: Inundation.
Meaning: Flooding of an area to create an obstacle.

Subject: Invest.
Meaning: To lay a siege or dominate an area with a force and isolate it.

Subject: Isolate.
Meaning: A tactical task given to a unit to seal off, both physically and psychologically, an enemy from his sources of support, deny him freedom of movement, and prevent his unit from having contact with other enemy forces.

Subject: J (Jour) Day.
Meaning: Used by French speaking countries and means D-Day.

Subject: Jamming.
Meaning: Jamming is the use of powerful transmissions to overwhelm an enemy receiver such that it is unable to receive wanted signals.

Subject: Javelin.
Meaning: Javelin is a shoulder launched anti-aircraft system designed to intercept directly attacking targets. It has a minimum range of 500m, maximum ranges of 4.5 kms (against approaching aircraft) and 5.5 kms(against hovering helicopters) and a maximum effective height of 3,000 feet. It can only be fired dismounted and can only be used by day. The recentintroduction of ADAD has significantly improved the early warning and target acquisition capability of Javelin detachments.

Subject: Jockeying.
Meaning: The movement of tanks to alternative positions in order to:a.Avoid detection.b.Avoid being engagedc.Gain some other tactical advantage.

Subject: Joint Air Attack Team (JAAT) Operations.
Meaning: A JAAT operation is a coordinatedattack involving a combination of aviation and OAS aircraft, normally supported by artillery or naval gunfire and, where possible, by Electronic Warfare (EW) assets. The combination of these elements provides a highly mobile force with a destructive capability which, if used correctly, can considerably influence the course of the ground battle. The purpose of a JAAT is to provide a commander with a flexible combination of firepower that can be utilised quickly across the battlefield.

Subject: Joint Force.
Meaning: A force made up of more than one service (Army, Navy and Air force). In a CRW environment the police are inclusive

Subject: Joint Operations.
Meaning: Operations involving more than one service (Army, Navy and Air force). This includes the police in a CRW setting.

Subject: Junction Point.
Meaning: Designated point at which in all types of combatunits/fmns must make contact for control and coordination.

Subject: K-Day.
Meaning: The day on which the convoy system is introduced on any particular convoy lane.

Subject: Key Point (KP)1.
Meaning: A concentrated site or installation, the destruction orcapture of which would seriously affect the war effort or the success of operations. E.g., ammunition dump.

Subject: Key Point (KP)2.
Meaning: In IS operation KPs are the priority Vulnerable Point (VP) which is classified as key and for which a militaryguard should be provided. The classification may be for a limited period only. Examples are:a.Communication centre.b.Joint HQs.c.Public utilities such as power stations and waterworks.d.Bridge essential to the security forces.

Subject: Key Terrain.
Meaning: A key terrain is any feature or area which the seizure or control offers a marked tactical advantage. Examples of key terrain features incl;bridges, fording site, high ground, choke points road junctions and survey control points.

Subject: Killing Area (KA).
Meaning: An area in which a commander plans to force the enemy to concentrate, so as to destroy him with conventional or tactical nuclearweapons. The area or zones where nuclear weapons are primarily planned to be used are termed nuclear killing zones (NKZ).

Subject: Knoll
Meaning: A knoll is a low detached hill.

Subject: L-Hour.
Meaning: a.The time when troops cross the start line for phase 2 in a phased attack. L-Hour is therefore to be associated with attacks that are of more than one phase.b.In amphibious and airmobile operations, L Hour is the time at which the first helicopter of a heliborne assault wave touches down inthe landing zone.

Subject: Land Force Elements.
Meaning:
A land force consists of combat, combat support,combat service support and command support elements. The proportion of each will vary between campaigns and operations.
a. Combat Element. Combat elements are those elements thatengage the enemy directly; they fight, typically employing direct-fire weapons. They include infantry, armoured and some aviation units.
 b. Combat Support Element. Combat Support is 'fire support and operational assistance provided to combat elements' Combat Support elements include: Arty fire support, air defence, reconnaissance, combat engineer, some aviation and some electronic warfare elements.
c. Combat Service Support. Combat Service Support is 'the support provided to combat forces primarily in the fields of administration and logistics'. These force elements include logistic,medical and equipment support; personnel welfare; and administration. Others are force support engineers, they provide water and electrical power supply, construct infrastructure andmaintain supply routes.

d. Command Support Element. Command Support elements assist commanders in the exercise of command. They include staff of all types; communications, intelligence and information systems; andlife support elements to protect, sustain and move the commanderand his staff.

Subject: Landing Craft.
Meaning: Seagoing craft which falls under the category ofamphibious shipping, designed to carry and land forces and their equipmentwith or without the use of aport.

Subject: Landing Point.
Meaning: A point within a landing site where one helicopter canland.

Subject: Landing Site.
Meaning: A site within a landing zone containing one or morelanding points. In amphibious operations,landing siteis a continuous segment of coastline over which troops, equipment and supplies can belanded by surface means.

Subject: Landing Zone (LZ).
Meaning: Any specified zone used for the landing of aircraftincluding troop lift aircraft.

Subject: Lateral Obstacles Belts.
Meaning: Obstacles laid across a frontage, the aim being tocut all routes through a zone extending across the enemy's line of advance,including any lateral routes which could be used to switch axes.

Subject: Latitude.
Meaning: The latitude of a place is the area of the meridian from the place to equator expressed in degrees at the centre of the Earth.

Subject: Layback Position.
Meaning: Temporary position occupied by one withdrawingsubunit to cover the withdrawal of another. Essentially the principle of 'one leg up one leg down', applied to withdrawal operations. It is only applicable today withdrawal.

Subject: Leadership.
Meaning: The art of influencing and directing men in such a manner as to obtain their willingness, loyalty, obedience and respect to accomplish amission.

Subject: Leaguer.
Meaning: A defended formation, sometimes concealed, adopted by a force for administrative convenience and protection. Usually associated witharmour. Leaguers may be close, with vehicles parked very near one another, or open, with vehicles wellspaced out.

Subject: Leap Frogging.
Meaning: Type of tactical movement used during mechanized and non mechanised operation. The rear vehicles/troops pass through the frontvehicles/troops on to the next fire position with the later providing covering fire. It is used where speed is essential andwhen enemy contact is not expected and risk can be taken.

Subject: Left Out of Battle (LOB).
Meaning: Personnel who are exempted from full combatduty with their units.

Subject: Levels of War.
Meaning: There are 3 levels of war; they are strategic, operational, and tactical.a. The strategic level.This includes both the grand strategy and the military strategy. Grand strategy is the application of national resources to achieve policy objectives while military strategy is the application of military resources to achieve grand strategic objectives.b. The operational level.This extends from the level of a joint task force including the combined forces of naval, air power and ground operation to the manoeuvre brigade echelon.c. The tactical level.This extends from the manoeuvre brigade to the lowest fighting elements including individual soldiers.

Subject: Levee en masse.
Meaning: Levee en masse are Inhabitants of a non-occupiedterritory, who on the approach of the enemy spontaneously and en masse take up arms to resist the invading forces, without having had time to formthemselves into organized armed units. Participants in a ''levee en masse'' are considered as combatants provided they carry arms openly and must respect the law of war.Leverage.Leverage inoperational art is gaining, maintaining, and exploiting advantages in combat power across all dimensions. Leverage allows joint force commanders to impose their will on the enemy, increase the enemy's dilemma, and maintain the initiative.

Subject: Liaison.
Meaning: Liaison is defined as that contact or intercommunication maintained between elements of military forces and, where necessary, nonmilitaryagencies to ensure mutual understanding and unity of purpose andaction.

Subject: Liaison Officer.
Meaning: A liaison officer is an officer who is exchanged between two or more forces and is empowered to represent and make appropriate recommendations on behalf of his commander. He has to be prepared toamplify his commander's intent and points of detail whenappropriate. Moreover, a liaison officer shall assist his own commander through the timelyexchange of information, intentions, and situational awareness.

Subject: Light Line.
Meaning: A designated line forward of which vehicles are required to use blackout lights at night.

Subject: Limited War.
Meaning: International armed conflicts, short of general war. It may be limited geographically, by the scale of forces or by the weapons employed but will be conducted overtly by formations of regular troops.

Subject: Linear Concentration.
Meaning: Type of artillery fire in which shells fall along anapproximate line on any desired bearing, for example, along the line of a trench system or the front edge of a wood. This takes longer to arrange than a simple Concentration and the response to correction is slower. (See ''Concentration1''.)

Subject: Linear Defence.
Meaning: A form of positional defence with little or no depth.

Subject: Lines of Communication.
Meaning: All the land, sea, and air routes that connect anoperating military force with one or more bases of operations, and along which supplies and reinforcements move.

Subject: Line of Departure (LD).
Meaning: In land warfare, a line designated to coordinate thedeparture of attack elements.

Subject: Lines of Logistic Support..
Meaning: Lines of Logistic Support refer to the level at which logistic support is controlled; they are as follows:a.First Line.Support integral to units; that is A and B echelon see ''Echelon'' for details.b.Second Line.Support within the division less first line. This encompasses CSS at both brigade and divisional level. In general, second line close support is found at the brigade level, and second line general support at divisional level.c.Third Line.In-theatre support to the rear of the division.

Subject: Lines of Operation.
Meaning: Lines of operation describe how military force is applied in time and space through decisive points on the path to the enemy centre ofgravity.

Subject: Link-Up operations.
Meaning: Link-Up operations are conducted to join two friendlyforces in enemy controlled territory. It may therefore be necessary to destroy the enemy between these forces before a link-up can be established. Bothforces maybe moving towards one another, or one may be stationary.

Subject: Location State (LOCSTAT).
Meaning: This is a location statement in the field, whichmust always be submitted by all units and formations immediately after every move, to the next higher HQ. A LOCSTAT must always show the exact location of the HQ originating the LOCSTAT and the HQ and/or area centre point of its subordinate formations or units. It is expressed as a sixfigure gridreference.

Subject: Local Magnetic Attraction.
Meaning: It is the deviation of the magnetic needle ofcompass from its main position, owing to the presence of masses of magnetic iron ore or of iron in the neighbourhood.

Subject: Logging.
Meaning: Logging is the most important part of a watch keeper's job.
