e. Tactical Control (TACON). TACON is the detailed and usually local direction and control of movement and manoeuvre necessary to accomplish missions or tasks assigned. This includes the coordination of real estate.
f. Under Command Administration (UCADMIN). This implies complete transfer of administrative/logistic command i.e. all services and personnel matters. It includes responsibility for all G1 matters including medical and provost.
g. Under Command for Admin (With Caveats) (UCADMIN...). When the temporary nature of the command makes it unnecessary to effect a complete change of administrative command, a formation or
unit may be placed under command for certain specific matters, or for administration less certain administrative matters.
h. Under Command for Daily Maintenance (UCDM). This state of command leaves the original parent formation or unit HQ with full responsibility for all administration less daily maintenance. The commander responsible for daily maintenance is responsible only for daily replenishment of combat supplies, evacuation of casualties, the provision of common user supply items and the repair and recovery of equipment.

Subject: Stock.
Meaning: A generic term conveying the quantities of items of materiel held on charge, as opposed to materiel in use.

Subject: Stragglers.
Meaning:
There are four types of stragglers:
a. Men who have genuinely lost their way and are attempting to rejoin their company group.
b. Men who, by reason of their mental and/or physical condition, cannot be held responsible for their actions.
c. Men running away through fear.
d. Men who, through no fault of their own, have become separated from their company group and are attempting to rejoin them.

Subject: Strategy.
Meaning:
a. Grand/National Strategy. The process of obilizing and directing in the most effective way all the resources of a nation including the armed forces to safeguard and promote its interests against those of its enemies, actual or potential. It is the application of national resources to achieve policy objectives.
b. Military Strategy. Military strategy is strictly concerned with the employment of military power during peace and in war to fulfil the aim of the grand strategy or foreign policy. In peacetime, it determines how military forces are deployed to deter war. In wartime, it involves producing the conditions under which tactical operations can take place and guides the employment of military forces in pursuit of victory.

Subject: Strike.
Meaning: See ''Core Functions of the Manoeuvrist Approach''.

Subject: Strong point1.
Meaning: Strong point is a heavily fortified position tied to a natural or reinforcing obstacle to create an anchor for the defence or to block a key piece of terrain.

Subject: Strong point2.
Meaning: Strong point in FIBUA is a section or a platoon post sited around a round intersection with fire positions in two or three different buildings with interlocking and mutually sp fire.

Subject: Sub-station.
Meaning: All other stations on a radio net apart from the control station. See 'Radio Station'.

Subject: Subject Indicator Code(SIC).
Meaning: A 3 letter group which identifies the subject matter of a message and provides delivery instructions for sig messages.

Subject: Subversion.
Meaning: Action taken to undermine the military, economic, psychological, morale or political strength of a nation and the loyalty of the subjects.

Subject: Summary and Abstracts of Evidence.
Meaning: The two methods of reducing evidence to writing are: Summary of Evidence and Abstracts of Evidence. Reducing evidence to writing may be necessary if for example, a CO investigating a case under certain circumstance, (like if the maximum punishment for the offence with which the accused is charged is death) before he submits the charge to higher authority, or hear the evidence himself.

Subject: Superimposed (Artillery) Fire Unit.
Meaning:
A fire unit, normally the direct support battery, tasked with providing additional fire on a target already allotted a fire unit; hence the word 'superimposed.' The idea is to:
a. Ensure that an objective allotted a superimposed fire unit is not left unattended when the superimposed fire unit if lifted for other tasks.
b. Prevent the direct support battery sitting idle while awaiting an impromptu or on call target.

Subject: Supplementary Intelligence Report (SUPINTREP).
Meaning: A detailed and comprehensive report which elaborates on intelligence collected over a period of time. Normally originated at divisional headquarters and above level with a controlled distribution. Preceded by the abbreviation SUPINTREP.

Subject: Supplies
Meaning: All materiel and items used in the equipment, support and maintenance of military forces.

Subject: Support.
Meaning: The action of a force, or portion thereof, which aids, protects, complements, or sustains any other force.

Subject: Support by Fire.
Meaning: A designated task in which a manoeuvre element moves to a position on the battlefield where it can engage the enemy by direct fire. The manoeuvre element does not attempt to manoeuvre to capture enemy forces or terrain.

Subject: Supporting Attack.
Meaning:
An offensive operation carried out in conjunction with
a main attack and designed to achieve one or more of the following:
a. Deceive the enemy.
b. Destroy or pin down enemy forces which could interfere with the main attack.
c. Control ground whose occupation by the enemy will hinder the main attack.
d. Force the enemy to commit reserves prematurely or in an indecisive area.

Subject: Supporting Fire.
Meaning: Fire delivered by supporting units to assist or protect a unit in combat.

Subject: Surprise and Security.
Meaning: Surprise makes a major contribution to the breaking of the enemy's cohesion and his defeat. It is achieved by doing the unexpected and thereby creating opportunities and gaining the initiative from the enemy. Its effect can be enhanced through the use of speed, secrecy and deception. Security involves maintaining the initiative and enhancing freedom of action by limiting vulnerability to hostile activities and threats.

Subject: Surveillance and Target Acquisition Plan (STAP).
Meaning: STAP enables battlegroup HQs to coordinate and control all available sensors in order to provide warning of the enemy's movement within their area of interest in sufficient time to react to it. The objective is to acquire the target that will be identified when it is in the location where your selected strike assets can most effectively be brought to bear.

Subject: Sustainability.
Meaning: The ability of a force to maintain the necessary level of combat power for the duration required to achieve the objective.

Subject: Sustainability Statement.
Meaning:
Sustainability Statement defines the level of CSS that is to be made available to a commander. A formal Sustainability Statement should always be prepared and be part of the overall planning for logistics when a force is to be deployed; it provides the basis for all subsequent CSS activities. It should at least include the following:
a. The expected duration of the deployment and the operation.
b. The quantity of ammunition that is required in theatre expressed in Days of Supply (DOS).
c. The quantity of all other materiel that is required in theatre.
d. The predicted casualty rate for men, either from battle or disease and non battle injuries; and equipment. e. Repair and recovery priorities by equipment and formation type.

Subject: Sustained Fire.
Meaning: Firing continuously.

Subject: Sweep.
Meaning: The thorough search of an area to ensure that no enemy remains undetected in it or is able to escape. This action is more peculiar to CRW operations.

Subject: Synchronization.
Meaning: Synchronization is the focusing of resources and activities to produce maximum combat power at the decisive time and place. The product of effective synchronisation is maximum economy of force, with every resources being used when and where it will make the greatest contribution to success.

Subject: Synchronisation Matrix.
Meaning: Synchronisation matrix links DSO with commander tactical plan by showing how the battle develops. It provides a useful graphical planning tool to assist the commander and his staff analysing own COA both in time and space in relation to the enemy's most likely COA. It should incorporate all offensive support, recce and manoeuvre. Production of the Synchronisation Matrix is a G3 function or the task of battlegroup 2IC at battle group level.

Subject: Synergy.
Meaning: In operational art, synergy is a concept that relates to integrating and synchronizing operations.

Subject: Tactical Air  Reconnaissance.
Meaning: Tactical air reconnaissance collects information on the enemy, weather and geographical features required for the planning and conduct of land operations.

Subject: Tactical Area of Operational Responsibility (TAOR).
Meaning: The TAOR is the area in which commander intends his force to manoeuvre; and in which the threat forces that will affect, or be affected by these operations are also expected to deploy.

Subject: Tactical Command.
Meaning: See 'State of Command'.

Subject: Tactical Control.
Meaning: See 'State of Command'.

Subject: Tactical Exercise Without Troops (TEWT).
Meaning: Exercise without troops aimed at teaching officers and SNCOs detailed application of tactical principles on the ground before the stage of an exercise with troops is reached. A TEWT must be framed to bring out certain definite lessons, e.g. the application of the principles of defence in a unit taking up a defensive position.

Subject: Tactical Operations.
Meaning:
Tactical operations are operations at the tactical level
and they are as follows:
a. Reconnaissance and Security.
b. Offensive Operations.
c. Defensive Operations.
d. Delay Operations.
e. Transitional Operations.

Subject: Tactical Minefield.
Meaning: See ''Minefield''.

Subject: Tactics.
Meaning: Tactics is the techniques for using the combination of weapons and units for engaging and defeating an enemy in battle. It is the art of using resources to their best advantage, taking into account the composition of own force, the ground over which it has to operate, the strength and disposition of the enemy and his likely reaction to own moves. It is essentially the employment of units in combat.

Subject: Tankable (Tank Going).
Meaning: Area of ground that is ''go and slow go'' to amour. The only ground not tankable is one over which it is physically impossible to move tanks even with engineer assistance.

Subject: Tank Harbour.
Meaning: An area where a tank unit or submit lies up for any length of time for a refit, maintenance and reorganization. It is usually well behind own Forward Defended Localities (FDLs) with concealment as the primary requirement. Also see Harbour.

Subject: Tank Hunting.
Meaning:
An action, similar to the laying of ambushes, whereby
tanks are destroyed by small parties of infantry using own weapons. Tank hunting teams of two men (or even one suitably armed soldier) can be organized to stalk and destroy an unprotected tank in a defensive locality.

Subject: Target Acquisition.
Meaning:
Target Acquisition is the process of collecting detailed
information about the location of enemy forces with sufficient accuracy to enable weapons systems to suppress or destroy those elements of the enemy selected as targets.

Subject: Target Area of Interest (TAI).
Meaning: A TAI is an area where the commander can influence the battle by destroying, delaying or disrupting the enemy. TAIs can be Point TAIs, e.g. a bridge, or Area TAIs, e.g. a valley.

Subject: Target Reference Point (TRP).
Meaning: An easily recognised point on the ground (either natural or manmade) used to initiate, distribute and control fire.

Subject: Target Selection Standard (TSS).
Meaning: TSS are criteria, applied to enemy activity (acquisitions and battlefield information), used in deciding whether the activity is a target. Targets meet accuracy and timeliness requirements for attack, while suspected targets must be confirmed before any attack.

Subject: Targeting.
Meaning: This is the acquisition of targets and their subsequent attack. It is the process of selecting targets and matching appropriate response to them taking into account operational requirements and capabilities.

Subject: Task Force.
Meaning: A temporary force task organized and equipped under one commander for a specific mission. The strength of a task force may lie between a reinforced battalion group and a division.

Subject: Task Organisation or Grouping.
Meaning:
This is by cross-attaching sub-units (companies and squadrons) with the battlegroups based on the formation commander's estimate of the situation and subsequent plan for the impending operation. Task organisation should be constructed so that the battlegroup commander and his sub-unit commanders are able to fight their deep, close and rear battles as well as provide recce and security functions. Any subunit or battlegroup organization should comprise the ability to:
a. Find and fix.
b. Manoeuvre ''” strike.
c. Echelon ''” momentum
d. Reserve ''” uncommitted.
This is known as the 'rule' of four.

Subject: Telephone Battle.
Meaning: An indoor exercise aimed at teaching staff work and procedures which commanders and their staff will be expected to carry out in HQ in the field. Two levels of HQ can be exercised at the same time, e.g. a brigade HQ and its battalion group HQ or a divisional HQ and his brigade HQ. A telephone battle should provide a setting in which staff officers seek record, analyse and pass information, issue orders and instructions. The main communication channel is through use of telephones.

Subject: Tempo.
Meaning: Tempo is the rate or rhythm of activity relative to the enemy, within tactical engagements and battles and between major operations. It incorporates the capacity of the force to effect the transition from one operation of war to another. Tempo consists of three elements; speed of decision, speed of execution and the speed of transition from one activity to another.

Subject: Termination.
Meaning: Termination is an essential component of strategy and operational art, whereby forces know when to terminate military operations and how to preserve achieved advantages.

Subject: Terrain.
Meaning: Terrain is the combination of natural features, built-up areas and infrastructure.

Subject: Terrain Analysis.
Meaning: The process of analysing the various terrain features, and categorising them as ''No Go, Slow Go and Go'' according to their predicted effect on the ability of the threat and friendly forces to manoeuvre over the ground.

Subject: Terrorism.
Meaning: A resort to violence by a dissident faction in order to intimidate and coerce people for political ends. This many manifest itself in sabotage and assassination by individuals or small groups, or in the form of ambushes or attacks on civilians or police by large bodies of terrorist. It can take place in either urban or rural areas.

Subject: Threat Evaluation (TE).
Meaning:
In conducting IPB, TE consists of a series of discrete actions aimed at identifying the threat's overall capability, based on his doctrine. It is concerned with producing the Doctrinal Overlay. It is a 5-part process of:
a. Finding the threat ''“ Where is he.
b. Identify the threat ''“ Who is he and what are his assets and strength.
c. Assessing the threat ''“ What is his combat effectiveness because that will affect how it is likely to operate.
d. Predicting the threat's likely COAs.''“ What is he likely to do based on his doctrine i.e. how he usually operate if he is not constrained by the terrain.
e. Displaying the threat's likely COAs.''“ this is producing separate doctrinal overlays for each COA showing the likely effect on friendly forces.

Subject: Threat Integration (TI).
Meaning: In conducting IPB, TI combines Battlefield Area Evaluation (BAE) with Threat Evaluation (TE) to show how the threat COAs and the friendly forces ability to counter (i.e. own COAs) will be affected by the terrain. TI produces Situation Overlays and Event Overlays.

Subject: Time Line.
Meaning: In conducting IPB, Time Line is a line on situation overlay which predicts the movement of threat forces at specific interval.

Subject: Top secret.
Meaning: See ''Security Classification''.

Subject: Total Asset Visibility.
Meaning: A concept whereby data from many sources is brought together to provide visibility of all assets thereby facilitating their control at the appropriate level of command.

Subject: Traffic Control Post (TCP).
Meaning: Military police post established for traffic control, usually for specified periods, e.g. during a road move or in a river crossing operation.

Subject: Trailer.
Meaning: Any towed vehicle that does not of itself process automotive power.

Subject: Training.
Meaning: The term 'training' covers every aspect of military activity designed to increase a soldier's knowledge of his military skills, his self-confidence and his physical and mental fitness for war.

Subject: Transitional Phases.
Meaning:
Transitional phases link the primary operations of war. They are as follows:
a. Advance to Contact. The advance to contact seeks to regain contact with the enemy under the most favourable conditions.
b. Meeting Engagement. A meeting engagement involves action between two moving forces.
c. Link-Up Operations. The aim of a link-up operation is to establish contact between two or more friendly units which may have the same or differing missions. They normally occur in enemy controlled territory.
d. Withdrawal. A withdrawal occurs when a force disengages from an enemy force in accordance with the will of its commander.
e. Relief Operations. Relief of troops in combat occurs when combat activities are taken over by one force from another. These are: Relief in place, Forward passage of lines and Rearward passage of lines.

Subject: Transmission Security.
Meaning: Transmission Security is that component of COMSEC which includes all measures designed to protect our radio transmissions from enemy interception, analysis and deception.

Subject: Transmit Time.
Meaning: The time that elapses between the auth for the transmission of a msg and its receipt of addresses.

Subject: Transport Scales.
Meaning:
a. First line. Unit transport which take over C Sups and other stores from second line transport at Dps.
b. Second line. ST transport for the maintenance of formations and units in the forwards areas.
c. Third line. ST transport under control or army/force/corps HQ.

Subject: Triage.
Meaning: The evaluation and classification of wounded for the purposes of treatment and evacuation. It consists of the immediate sorting of patients according to type and seriousness of injury, and likelihood of survival, and the establishment of priority for treatment and evacuation to assure medical care of the greatest benefit to the largest number. Triage is also the evaluation and classification of equipment for the purpose of repairs or evacuation.

Subject: Umpire Organization.
Meaning:
That organization in an FTX whose tasks is to give
those being exercised a realistic impression of battle conditions, arbitrate between exercised troops and the controlled enemy when the former are attacked, assess damage and casualties and generally keep control informed of presents and future situations (see control organization).

Subject: Uncharged
Meaning: A demolition target which has been prepared to receive charges, the charges being packaged and stored in a safe place.

Subject: Unclassified.
Meaning: Refers to information and material that bears no security classification and therefore does not require any authority to be disclosed.

Subject: Unicode.
Meaning:
A letter substitute code used to conceal temporarily the grid reference of a place referred to while carrying voice conversation within units.
It is not used with slide.

Subject: Under Command for Administration (UCADMIN).
Meaning: See 'State of Command'.

Subject: Under Command for Daily Maintenance (UCDM).
Meaning: See 'State of Command'.

Subject: Undulating Ground.
Meaning: Ground, which alternatively rises and falls gently.

Subject: Unit Deplaning Officer.
Meaning: A unit officer trained as an assistant UEO (see), for the deplaning and unloading of his unit after an air move. He normally moves with the unit advance party and therefore cannot also act as the UEO.

Subject: Unit Emplaning Officer (UEO).
Meaning:
An officer in the unit trained to be responsible for supervising the emplaning and loading of the unit into an aircraft. He is also responsible for:
a. Training the unit in all aspects of air movement including the use of helicopters.
b. Preparing and maintaining the unit air staff table.
c. Supervising the packaging and preparation of unit stores and equipment.

Subject: Unit Equipment Table.
Meaning: A unit equipment table shows the details of all equipment which is authorized for a unit to hold.

Subject: Unit Mobile Stocks (UMS).
Meaning: That element of First Line stocks that can be carried on unit transport.

Subject: Unit Repair Scale (URS).
Meaning: A scaling of spares which are in frequent demand for repairs being carried out by unit or attached repair tradesmen.

Subject: Vanguard.
Meaning: See 'Advance Guard'.

Subject: Vehicles.
Meaning:
Vehicles in the military are categorised as follows:
a. 'A' Vehicles. A' Vehicles are vehicles which are armoured and may be designed to carry offensive armament. This category includes specialist 'A' vehicles such as armoured engineer and
recovery vehicles and APCs.
b. 'B' Vehicles. 'B' Vehicles are unarmoured vehicles of all types including trailers; they are often referred to as soft skinned vehicles/
c. 'C' Vehicles. 'C' Vehicles are mobile items of earth moving equipment and all types of crawler, wheeled and truck mounted cranes and mechanical handling equipment.
d. 'D' Vehicles. 'D' Vehicles are amphibious vehicles designed for landing troops on beaches.
e. 'E' Vehicles. 'E' vehicles are basic B vehicles fitted with specialist equipment, e.g. Fitted for Radio (FFR) Land rover

Subject: Veiled Speech.
Meaning: The art of referring to the future by reference to past events of which the enemy has no knowledge of, e.g., ''send your sunray at the same time and place as yesterday.'' Veiled speech provides good security, provided it is not overdone.

Subject: Vertical Take Off and Landing (VTOL).
Meaning: The capability of an aircraft to take ''“ off and land vertically and to transfer to or from forward motion at heights required to clear surrounding obstacles.

Subject: Vital Ground.
Meaning: Ground of such tactical importance that it must be retained or controlled for the success of the mission.

Subject: Vulnerable Points (VP).
Meaning:
VPs are those points where it is particularly advantageous for the adversary to position an ambush, using bombs, bobby traps, or IEDs. Likely places are:
a. Culverts.
b. Bridges.
c. High banked stretches of road.
d. Routes dominated by high ground (possible firing points).
e. Junctions.
f. Buildings and walls near route.
g. Parked vehicles.
h. Prominent markers on routes (e.g. poles and road signs).
I. Location of previous attack.
j. Places where vehicles slow down (bends, potholes, debris, traffic calming areas).
k. Places where road narrows.

Subject: War Crime.
Meaning: War crimes are violation of laws of war; they are crime committed during wartime that is in violation of international agreements concerning the conventions of war, e.g. the mistreatment of prisoners or genocide.

Subject: War Reserves.
Meaning:
Stocks of materiel amassed in peacetime to meet the
increase in military requirements consequent upon an outbreak of war. War reserves are intended to provide the interim support to sustain operations until resupply can be effected.

Subject: War Wastage Rate.
Meaning:
These are rate that lay down the wastage for all items
of equipment vehicle and stores. They form the basis for provisioning for the army and for stocking the corps maintenance areas.

Subject: War gaming.
Meaning: War gaming are simulations in which theories of warfare can be tested and refined without the need for actual hostilities. It can be anything from a computer driven analysis to a demonstration on a sand model or map. In the Commander's Estimate Process, war gaming is used to develop the detailed plan by comparing the COA determined by the commander with the most likely enemy COAs identified through the IPB process. It achieves this by helping the commander and his staff to visualise the flow of the operation.

Subject: Warhead.
Meaning: That part of the missile, projectile and torpedo rocket or other ammunition which contains either the nuclear or thermonuclear system, high explosive system chemical or biological agents or insert material intended to inflict damage.

Subject: Warning Order.
Meaning: A warning order may be written, graphical or oral. It should initiate battle procedure. Warning orders should be issued as soon as possible and should not be delayed because all the information e.g. definitive tasks are not currently available. The warning order can be updated as information becomes available.

Subject: Watercourse.
Meaning: The line defining the lowest of a valley, occupied by a stream.

Subject: Water shed.
Meaning: A ridge of land separating two drainage basins that is, the summit of land which water divides of flows in two different directions. A watershed normally includes the highest point of a chain of mountains or range of hills.

Subject: Weapons Engagement Zone (WEZ).
Meaning:
A WEZ is airspace of defined dimensions where the responsibility for engagement rests with a particular
weapon system. Some examples of WEZs include:
a. Fighter Engagement Zone (FEZ). For land based AD, a FEZ is airspace of defined dimensions where the responsibility for engagement of air threats normally rests with fighter aircraft.
b. Joint Engagement Zone (JEZ). A JEZ is airspace of specific dimensions where friendly SAMs and fighters are simultaneously employed
c. Short Range Air Defence Engagement Zone (SHORADEZ). ASHORADEZ is airspace of defined dimensions where the responsibility for engagement rests with short-range air defence weapons.

Subject: Weapons Free.
Meaning: See ''Air Defence Weapons Control Status''.

Subject: Weapons Hold
Meaning: See ''Air Defence Weapons Control Status''.

Subject: Weapons Tight.
Meaning: See ''Air Defence Weapons Control Status''.

Subject: Weapons Unlimited.
Meaning: See ''Air Defence Weapons Control Status''.

Subject: Wedge.
Meaning:
The punching of a hole in enemy's forward by an armoured force, the aim being to create a reasonable secure corridor through which the induction of follow up echelon may be accomplished for subsequent
development of depth operations.

Subject: Wider Peacekeeping.
Meaning: This is the wider part of peacekeeping carried out with consent of the belligerent parties, but in an environment that may be highly volatile.

Subject: Withdrawal.
Meaning: A withdrawal is when a force disengages from the enemy either in or out of contact with the enemy in accordance with the will of its superior commander. Although contact may be maintained through other means such as indirect fire, reconnaissance or surveillance.

Subject: Zones of Fire.
Meaning: Zones of fire are assigned to fire support units for control of fire laterally and in depth to support operations.

Subject: Zone Time.
Meaning:
The earth is divided into 25 time zones, some ahead of GMT, and others behind. The Zone Time is that of a particular area relative to GMT. Each zone time is given a letter called the 'zone time suffix'. The zone time suffixes area as follow:
A + 1 (e.g. Nigeria)
B + 2
C + 3
D + 4
E + 5
F + 6
G + 7
H + 8
I + 9
K + 10
L + 11
M + 12
N - 1
O - 2
P - 3
Q - 4
R - 5
S - 6
T - 7
U - 8
V - 9
W - 10
X - 11
Y - 12
Z (GMT)
To get area with half hourly differences, two letters area are combined e.g. The zone time suffix of an area 41/2 hours ahead of GMT will be DE. Observe the letter J is missing in this arrangement.

Subject: Zulu Muster.
Meaning: A conceal area where Zulu Vehicles (see) proceed to and wait during the assault.

Subject: Zulu Vehicles.
Meaning: Empty APCs, from which assaulting troops have dismounted. Zulu Vehicles remain in a Zulu Muster (see) until called forward.
